latest_release.name: v2.7.0
latest_release.body:
This release marks one of Quarkdown's most significant milestones towards becoming a mature, community-driven project!

 

### Added

 

#### [Packages & package manager](https://quarkdown.com/wiki/packages)

This release comes with Quarkdown's long-awaited package manager! You can browse the available packages in the new [catalog](https://studio.quarkdown.com/atoms).

A package, called **_atom_**, can be easily included into your document the same way you `.include` any other local Quarkdown file, with the special syntax `@scope/name:version`.

The officially maintained scope, [`@atoms`](https://github.com/quarkdown-labs/atoms), is a GitHub-hosted repository anyone can contribute to.

```markdown
.include {@atoms/cowsay:1.0.0}

.cowsay {Hello, Quarkdown!}
```

We can't wait to see your creations!

 

#### [Project templates from packages](https://quarkdown.com/wiki/publishing-packages#templates)

`quarkdown create` can now scaffold a project from a template package, via the new `--template` option:

    quarkdown create --template @atoms/simple-cv:1.0.0

 

#### Linux-ARM support

Quarkdown now runs on Linux-aarch64!

Thanks @maximilianbarg!

 

#### [Styling options on `.row`, `.column` and `.grid`](https://quarkdown.com/wiki/stacks)

Stack functions now accept the same styling options as `.container`, such as `background`, `foreground`, `border`, `padding`, `radius` and the font options, along with `width` and `height`, without relying on container wrapping.

```markdown
.row gap:{1cm} width:{12cm} background:{teal} foreground:{white} padding:{12px} radius:{8px}
    A

    B
```

 

#### [Scoped page formatting in slides](https://quarkdown.com/wiki/page-format)

The `pages` and `side` parameters of `.pageformat`, previously available only in `paged` documents, now also work in `slides` documents. A scoped format applies its properties to the selected slides only.

```markdown
.pageformat pages:{2..3} background:{navy} alignment:{start}
```

 

#### [Page content padding](https://quarkdown.com/wiki/page-format)

`.pageformat` accepts a new `padding` parameter, which adds blank space inside the content area of each page, between its borders and the content.

```markdown
.pageformat padding:{1cm} bordercolor:{red}
```

 

#### [Color building and derivation](https://quarkdown.com/wiki/color)

The new `.color` function builds a color from its red, green, blue and alpha components, each optional, and a base color:

```markdown
.var {brand} {red}

.container background:{.brand::color alpha:{0.25}}
```

 

#### [New boolean operations: `and` and `or`](https://quarkdown.com/wiki/boolean#operators)

The new `and` and `or` functions combine two boolean values, complementing the existing `not`.

```markdown
.if {.x::islower than:{10}::and {.x::isgreater than:{0}}}
    x is between 0 and 10
```

 

#### [New collection operation: `contains`](https://quarkdown.com/wiki/boolean#operators)

The new `contains` function checks whether a string contains some text, a collection contains an element, or a dictionary contains a key.

```markdown
.var {letters}
    - A
    - B

.if {.letters::contains {B}}
    B is in the list
```

 

#### [New collection operation: `withindices`](https://quarkdown.com/wiki/loops#indices)

The new `withindices` function turns a collection into a dictionary that maps each element's position, starting at 1, to the element itself.
This makes numbered iteration straightforward.

```markdown
.var {letters}
    - A
    - B

.letters::withindices::foreach
    index letter:
    .index .letter
```

> Output:
> 1 A
> 2 B
